data.why: The app has no bundled dataset and reads a data folder by local path (not browser upload), so synthetic Vicon-style COP/COM trial files for one subject (Control_001, Acute + SubAcute) were written straight into the repo's expected folder/filename layout, along with a short-duration custom stimulus config so the small files don't need 120 s/1000 Hz of data.

goals: Load a folder of postural-sway trial recordings and confirm the pipeline discovers and parses all expected files
Compute the frequency-response function (gain, phase, coherence) at each stimulus frequency for standing and walking trials
Compare gain/phase across groups, amplitudes, and the Acute→SubAcute→Chronic recovery trajectory
Compute per-trial summary sway metrics (RMS, path length, mean velocity) and compare across conditions
Export the FRF and summary-metrics results as CSVs for downstream statistical analysis
Re-run the pipeline after adding new subject files and confirm caching only reprocesses new trials

review.summary: The goal and phases capture what the README says this tool is for: sum-of-sines visual-perturbation FRF and sway metrics per trial, compared across groups and recovery stages, then exported. The cited screens back up the nodes. It needs fixes before filing: mislabelled branches, error probes and an accident mixed into the workflow, a too-broad viewer feature, and a summary-CSV row count that contradicts the replay and hides a duplication bug in the cached re-run.
